public_source.title: Improved bounds on the supremum of autoconvolutions
public_source.notes: The paper explicitly calls this the best step-function example then known for the second autoconvolution inequality at n=20 and prints all 20 nonnegative coefficients in the online appendix. The support is [-1/4, 1/4]. Boyer and Li (2025, arXiv:2506.16750, Sections 2-3) independently transcribe the same 20 coefficients, state n=20, and recompute the score as 0.889226. The local checker recomputes the exact rational score from the printed finite decimals. The 2009 paper says the example was not extensively optimized; it does not claim a global optimum over 20-step functions.

T080-C01.comparison_tolerance: Witness-level identity: coefficients match the 20-entry Matolcsi-Vinuesa appendix witness as independently transcribed by Boyer-Li. The source prints only 0.88922...; the exact local score is recomputed from those printed finite decimal coefficients.
limitations: Best located same-parameter public construction, not a proof of optimality among all 20-step functions. Matolcsi-Vinuesa state they did not make extensive efforts to optimize this example.

This is a finite source comparison of the original Matolcsi-Vinuesa appendix and later directly relevant AlphaEvolve, Boyer-Li, Jaech-Joseph, SimpleTES, and DREAM-RSI reports. It does not establish that every public source has been surveyed.

The Matolcsi-Vinuesa appendix gives decimal coefficients rather than exact rational coefficients. Exactness here means exact arithmetic on those printed finite decimals, not recovery of hidden higher-precision values.
The inspected DREAM-RSI paper reports its first autocorrelation inequality result, not a separate result for the second autocorrelation inequality (T080).

The 2009 source does not describe the numerical search algorithm, random seed, or compute budget that produced its 20-step coefficients. This reproduction uses the printed witness directly and does not invent those missing details.

reproduction_method.method: Read the 20 printed decimal heights from the Matolcsi-Vinuesa appendix witness file and rescore them with the T080 exact rational checker.
reproduction_method.source_search_details: The paper reports a numerical search and states it did not make extensive efforts to optimize this example; it gives no algorithm, seed, or budget. No new search result is claimed here.

best_located_same_parameter.source: Matolcsi-Vinuesa 2009 online appendix; 20 printed coefficients; coefficient list and score independently confirmed by Boyer-Li 2025, arXiv:2506.16750

highest_located_report_any_step_count.parameter_note: The paper reports the AC2 result and describes the AC2 search as FFT plus L-BFGS-B over sparse witnesses. It does not specify a 20-step witness; this is a different-resolution result, not T080-C01.

comparison_scope.evidence: Authors call this the best 20-step example then known and print 20 coefficients.

comparison_scope.source: AlphaEvolve, Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale
comparison_scope.evidence: Boyer-Li directly identify the AlphaEvolve witness as 50 equal intervals.

comparison_scope.source: Boyer-Li, An improved example for an autoconvolution inequality
comparison_scope.evidence: Theorem 1 and Appendix A give 575 coefficients; Section 3 compares the n=20 Matolcsi-Vinuesa witness and reports its recomputed score 0.889226.

comparison_scope.source: Jaech-Joseph, Further Improvements to the Lower Bound for an Autoconvolution Inequality
comparison_scope.evidence: Abstract states 2,399 intervals for one construction and obtains 0.94136 by 4x upsampling a 559-interval optimizer (2,236 intervals).

comparison_scope.source: AlphaEvolve V2, reported in SimpleTES Appendix O.1
comparison_scope.evidence: SimpleTES Appendix O.1 table reports the value; TTT-Discover's related-work summary identifies the AlphaEvolve V2 construction as 50,000 pieces.

comparison_scope.source: SimpleTES, Structured Scaling of AI Discovery Across Diverse Scientific Domains
comparison_scope.evidence: Appendix O.1 reports AC2 score and says its best program uses FFT evaluation and L-BFGS-B refinement on sparse witnesses; the paper does not report a 20-step witness.

comparison_scope.source: DREAM-RSI, Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds
comparison_scope.evidence: Its paper reports the first autocorrelation inequality, with lower-is-better scores around 1.45; it does not report a T080 second-autocorrelation score.

related_public_reports.parameter_note: Reported using a 50,000-piece step function; not 20 steps. Earlier AlphaEvolve result was 0.8962 with 50 steps.
Reported for AC2 without a matching 20-step specification; its published search description is FFT and L-BFGS-B over sparse witnesses.
Its comparison table reports first autocorrelation, not the T080 second-autocorrelation task.

verification.source_review: Reviewed original Matolcsi-Vinuesa appendix and Boyer-Li2025 primary paper. The latter explicitly identifies the MV20, AE50 and BL575 grids. The strongest located same-20-step public witness is the archived MV coefficient list; its exact ratio is independently recomputed. This is a finite source comparison, not an optimality proof.
